children: United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket failed to deliver 40 Amazon
Leo internet satellites into orbit Sunday, dealing a setback to Amazon’s broadband ambitions and the launch provider’s efforts to establish its new rocket.
ULA said the malfunction occurred about 10 minutes
from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The company, jointly owned by Boeing
and Lockheed Martin
, will investigate the cause and determine what repairs are needed before flights resume.
For investors, the failure raises the prospect of additional costs and delays as Amazon
builds a satellite network to compete with SpaceX’s
Starlink. A prolonged interruption could postpone revenue opportunities for Amazon Leo and put pressure on ULA’s launch business, although the financial impact remains unclear.
The mission was Vulcan’s fifth flight and its first carrying Amazon satellites. Amazon
has purchased 38 Vulcan launches, making the rocket an important part of its deployment plans. ULA previously carried Leo satellites on eight Atlas 5 missions.
Amazon’s
planned constellation requires more than 3,300 satellites. Sunday’s launch would have brought its cumulative total launched to 436. The company also has launch agreements with SpaceX
, Europe’s Ariane 6 and Blue Origin, spreading deployment across several providers.

That strategy faces another constraint: Blue Origin’s New Glenn remains sidelined following a launchpad explosion in May. Vulcan had also gone nine months between flights while ULA and Northrop Grumman
addressed booster nozzle problems observed on earlier missions.

The solid rocket boosters appeared to operate normally Sunday. The failure occurred during the Centaur upper stage’s firing, according to ULA’s reported timeline, but the company hasn't identified the underlying cause. Earlier countdown interruptions have not been linked to the loss.
Amazon

expressed continued confidence in ULA, which pledged to work with its customer and other organizations on the investigation. The failure was ULA’s first outright mission loss since its formation in 2006, adding uncertainty to the schedule for the rocket intended to replace Atlas 5.

title: Rocket failure destroys 40 Amazon satellites, threatening broadband rollout
